requirements.text: A MS or PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Mathematics, Physics, Robotics, or another highly quantitative discipline, or equivalent research or engineering experience.
Strong proficiency in Python (at least 3 years of experience) and experience building substantial machine-learning, scientific, or technical software.
Deep experience with PyTorch, JAX, or equivalent modern machine-learning frameworks.
Strong understanding of modern deep learning, including optimization, representation learning, sequence modeling, and latent-variable models.
Experience implementing and training nontrivial neural architectures from research papers.
Strong foundations in probability, linear algebra, optimization, numerical methods, and algorithms.
Experience working with sequential or temporally structured data.
Familiarity with state-space models, sequential latent-variable models, recurrent architectures, or model-based learning.
The ability to read mathematical or theoretical research and translate it into working implementations.
Experience designing experiments capable of validating or falsifying technical hypotheses.
Strong debugging skills across model architecture, training dynamics, numerical computation, data, and experimental infrastructure.
Experience with GPU-based training and performance optimization.
The ability to work autonomously while collaborating closely with a multidisciplinary research team.

Deep hands-on experience with learned state-space models or an adjacent class of sequential latent models, strong engineering ability, and the capacity to learn unfamiliar technical domains quickly matter more than breadth across the entire world-model literature.
Maintain high standards for code quality, testing, reproducibility, experimental design, and documentation.

We are not looking for someone who can only propose interesting architectures and hand their implementation to somebody else. You should be capable of independently turning research ideas into working experimental systems.
